message.content:
The quadratic equation  

\[
3x^{2}-2x-5=0
\]

has roots found with the quadratic formula \(x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}\).

Here \(a=3,\; b=-2,\; c=-5\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta &= b^{2}-4ac \\
       &= (-2)^{2}-4(3)(-5) \\
       &= 4+60 \\
       &= 64 .
\end{aligned}
\]

So

\[
x=\frac{-(-2)\pm\sqrt{64}}{2(3)}=\frac{2\pm8}{6}.
\]

Thus the two roots are

\[
x=\frac{2+8}{6}=\frac{10}{6}=\boxed{\tfrac53}\quad\text{and}\quad
x=\frac{2-8}{6}=\frac{-6}{6}=\boxed{-1}.
\]
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Solve for the roots of the equation 3x^2 - 2x - 5." They want the roots of the quadratic equation 3x^2 - 2x - 5 = 0. We can solve using quadratic formula: x = [2 ± sqrt( (-2)^2 - 4*3*(-5) )] / (2*3). Compute discriminant: b^2 - 4ac = 4 + 60 = 64. sqrt(64)=8. So x = [2 ± 8]/6. So solutions: (2+8)/6=10/6=5/3 ≈ 1.6667; (2-8)/6=-6/6=-1. So roots: x = 5/3 and x = -1.

We might also mention that we used the quadratic formula. Provide answer. No tool needed.
